newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARIAN BANKS SIGN $240MLN EXPORT FINANCING DEAL.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARIAN BANKS SIGN $240MLN EXPORT FINANCING DEAL.

text.p: Hungary's Eximbank signed an agreement on Friday on a $240 million preferential export refinancing credit line with 20 Hungarian commercial banks.
"The bank will offer very favourable loan conditions at the expense of its profit," Eximbank's General Manager Ivan Nyiri told a news conference after the signing.
State-owned Eximbank was set up in 1994 with the aim of promoting Hungarian exports.
Commercial banks are offered funds for short and medium-term refinancing of exports under two different schemes, Nyiri said.
The first scheme offers loans to commercial banks for periods shorter than two years at a floating interest rate of 0.5 percentage points below the three-month LIBOR (London Inter-Bank Offered Rate).
These loans can then be passed on to exporters with a maximum 1.5 percent mark-up.

Under the second scheme loans for periods of over two years will be offered to commercial banks at CIRR (Commercial Interest Reference Rate) minus 1.5 percentage points and the banks can pass them on at maximum the CIRR rate.
The CIRR rate is set monthly by the OECD and published weekly by Eximbank.
Commercial banks can offer loans of up to $5 million for the export of products with a minimum 50 percent domestic production or service content.

Nyiri said that only a "small percentage" of last year's 16 billion forints available under a similar scheme was actually used but this year's favourable terms would probably lead to the full usage of the available amount.
He added that the bank plans to spend 200 million to 400 million forints on these preferential loans.
Eximbank has a five billion forints issued share capital and in 1996 it had a balance sheet total of 5.2 billion forints.
According to customs statistics, Hungary's exports grew to $16 billion in 1996 from $12.9 billion in 1995, while the trade deficit widened to $2.7 billion in 1996 from $2.6 billion the year before.
